extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) establishes two conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems: internal control under Annex VI, or quality management system plus technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometric identification), the provider may use internal control or must use the notified body procedure under Annex VII, depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied.

Annex VII (notified body assessment) is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI; most other high-risk AI systems may use the Annex VI self-assessment route.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU product-safety legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures under that legislation, with notified bodies also verifying compliance with AI-specific requirements.
Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Under Article 46, a market surveillance authority may, upon justified request and for exceptional reasons of public security, life/health protection, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets, authorise placing a high-risk AI system on the market without the Article 43 conformity assessment, for a limited period.

Under Article 43, the provider may choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except that where the high-risk AI system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.

Article 44 governs certificates, Article 45 governs information obligations of notified bodies, Article 47 the EU declaration of conformity, and Article 48 CE marking, all part of Section 5 (Standards, Conformity Assessment, Certificates, Registration) of the AI Act.

Annex VII, section 4.5, allows a notified body, after exhausting other reasonable means and upon reasoned request, to be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system, including relevant parameters, to assess conformity with Chapter III Section 2 requirements.
Article 43(5) gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to update Annex VI and Annex VII in light of technical progress.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies under the AI Act.

A Council document (document ST-7322-2026-INIT) references a scope-of-designation scheme for conformity assessment bodies notified under 'Article 30' of 'this Regulation', listing AI system categories (AIP codes) tied to Annex I subsections.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) proposes creating a new Annex XIV listing categories and types of AI systems for the Commission's NANDO notified-body information system, and amending Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements.

As of October 2025, the NANDO system lists 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies, but this concerns medical device regulations (MDR/IVDR), not the AI Act specifically.
As of March 2026, no AI Act-specific notified body ecosystem was yet established; designation processes were described as ongoing across Member States with limited capacity and uncertain timelines.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies were formally designated under the AI Act for medical-device-related AI systems.

A news source states that under the 'final text agreed in September 2026,' the application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations was moved to 2 August 2029 from a previously reported 2 December 2027 date, citing that harmonised standards and notified bodies were still not ready.

A second news source (dated 2026-09-22) states that Annex III high-risk obligations apply from 2 August 2029, following a 'second amendment of Article 113' that replaced a 2 December 2027 date set by the 'AI Omnibus', and that providers will not need notified body conformity assessment for these systems until then.

A third source (dated 2026-09-29) describes the EU institutions as having 'deferred' the application of high-risk requirements for Annex III systems to 2 August 2029, noting this gives time for harmonised standards and first notified body designations to occur before conformity assessment begins.

A separate industry source states that 'August 2026' is the deadline by which high-risk AI obligations fully apply, and that post-2026, notified bodies designated under the AI Act will begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments.
Another compliance source states providers must issue an EU Declaration of Conformity, referencing the conformity assessment procedure followed (Annex VI or Annex VII), 'before August 2, 2026'.
An industry blog (undated) states the 'August 2026 deadline isn't moving' regarding notified body engagement for AI Act conformity assessments.

Interpretation: the dependence of the conformity assessment route on AI system type and deployment context means many public summaries of the Act's conformity assessment rules oversimplify by not distinguishing Annex III point 1 (biometrics) from other Annex III categories.
Interpretation: notified bodies are independent third-party organisations designated by Member States to perform conformity assessment procedures.

By analogy to the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated under that separate regulation's NANDO database, and a target of 11 December 2026 was set for sufficient notified body capacity, illustrating broader EU-wide delays in operationalizing third-party conformity assessment for new digital/product regulations.

This reflects either outdated information in the industry sources or a disputed/unverified claim of a later legislative amendment in the 2026-09 news sources, which do not cite a specific legal instrument number with certainty.

open_issues: No official EU legal source (EUR-Lex consolidated AI Act text or Official Journal publication) in the provided sources confirms whether the Annex III high-risk deadline was actually changed from 2 December 2027 to 2 August 2029; only secondary news/blog sources make this claim.

The exact current list of notified bodies designated specifically under the EU AI Act (as opposed to MDR/IVDR or CRA) is not provided by any source; the sources discuss NANDO designations for other regulations (MDR, IVDR, CRA) but do not confirm any AI Act-specific designations to date.

It is unclear how Article 30 (referenced in document ST-7322-2026-INIT) relates to the AI Act's own Article 43/Annex VII framework, since the AI Act itself does not have an Article 30 on notified body designation scope; sources do not clarify whether this is a different regulation or a renumbering proposal.
The relationship and conflict (if any) between the proposed COM(2025) 836 Annex XIV and the existing Annex VI/VII framework for conformity assessment is not explained in the sources.

No source specifies which Member States have operational AI Act notified body designation processes, how many bodies have applied, or expected designation timelines beyond general statements that none exist yet as of early-to-mid 2026.

Sources do not clarify whether the apparent 2029 deadline (sources 15, 20, 26) is a formal legislative amendment, a proposal still under negotiation, or a misinterpretation/rumor, since none cite the Official Journal or a consolidated EUR-Lex text reflecting this change.

It remains unclear which specific Annex III categories require mandatory notified body (Annex VII) assessment versus internal control (Annex VI), beyond biometric identification, since sources give only partial or generalized lists (e.g., 'certain critical infrastructure AI').
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) is generally reported to establish two principal conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems—internal control (Annex VI) and notified body assessment involving quality management and technical documentation review (Annex VII)—though this characterization rests on low-authority, undated sources (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment); [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU sectoral product-safety legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43); [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)). However, no source confirms that any notified bodies have yet been formally designated specifically under the AI Act, and significant uncertainty and contradiction exists regarding the compliance timeline for Annex III high-risk systems (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act); [AI Act Medical Devices Guide](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Industry sources describe Article 43 as establishing two main pathways: internal control under Annex VI, or a quality management system combined with technical documentation assessment by a notified body under Annex VII; however, this characterization derives from low-authority, undated industry blogs rather than official EU guidance and is rated low confidence (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment); [Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)). For Annex III point 1 systems (biometric identification), providers may use internal control or must use the notified body procedure depending on whether harmonised standards or common specifications have been applied (low confidence) ([futurium.ec.europa.eu](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). More broadly, Annex VII assessment is reported as mandatory for biometric identification and certain critical infrastructure AI, with most other high-risk systems eligible for Annex VI self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

By contrast, for high-risk AI systems already covered by sectoral EU product-safety legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) listed in Annex I Section A, providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements — a claim drawn from the official EU AI Act Service Desk and corroborated by industry analysis (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43); [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Procedural Rules
Substantial modifications generally require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 43](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Under Article 46, market surveillance authorities may, for exceptional public security or safety reasons, authorise market placement without conformity assessment for a limited period (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 46](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Providers may generally choose any notified body for Annex VII assessment, except where the system is intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority performs the notified body role (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk - Article 43 (GA)](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)).
